title: PostgreSQL/Aurora metadata backend
description:
Add PostgreSQL as an optional metadata backend alongside SQLite, targeting AWS Marketplace deployments where customers want managed RDS (Aurora Serverless v2) instead of self-managed SQLite files.

Why this issue exists:
sqlx already supports PostgreSQL — the driver is a feature flag away. The blocking work is:
1. Making the database URL in each config file point to either sqlite:// or postgres://
2. Rewriting the migration files from SQLite dialect to PostgreSQL dialect (or maintaining dual sets)
3. Removing WAL-mode pragmas (PostgreSQL doesn't use them) and SQLite-specific types (BLOB → BYTEA, INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT → BIGSERIAL)
4. Testing against a local PostgreSQL instance and against Aurora Serverless v2

Target deployment:
- AWS Marketplace listing: customer deploys on their own AWS account
- Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 for the metadata plane (core.db, transit.db, reader.db)
- mail.db can also use Aurora or stay SQLite depending on operator preference
- Signing key moves to AWS Secrets Manager (see persistent signing key epic)
- Transit gossipsub identity key can also live in Secrets Manager

Horizontal scaling coordination (required for multi-instance deployments with shared PostgreSQL + S3):

GC leader election:
- Only one transit instance should run GC at a time to avoid racing to unpin the same articles
- Use PostgreSQL advisory locks (pg_try_advisory_lock) to elect a GC leader at each scheduled run
- Non-leader instances skip the run and log a debug message
- Lock is released immediately after GC completes so leadership rotates naturally

HLC node_id per instance:
- With multiple transit instances sharing the same operator signing key, group log entries must still be distinguishable by instance
- Derive HLC node_id from instance ID (hostname, pod name, or a UUID generated at startup and stored in PostgreSQL) rather than from the signing key
- This ensures concurrent appends from different instances have distinct node_ids and do not produce HLC collisions

IPNS publisher:
- Multiple transit instances racing to publish the same IPNS name will stomp each other
- For multi-instance deployments, IPNS publishing must be restricted to a single elected publisher (same pg_try_advisory_lock pattern as GC) or disabled entirely
- Document in RUNBOOK.md: IPNS is not meaningful in a multi-instance deployment; group log tips are the canonical discovery mechanism

Out of scope:
- Multi-tenancy (one Aurora instance per customer is fine)
- Data migration tooling from SQLite to PostgreSQL (manual export/import is acceptable for v1)
- Replacing the CID block store with S3 (separate epic)

Acceptance criteria:
- Both sqlite:// and postgres:// URLs work at runtime; the backend is selected by the database URL in config
- All four databases (core, transit, reader, mail) have PostgreSQL-dialect migration files
- Integration tests pass against both SQLite (in-memory, existing) and PostgreSQL (docker-compose)
- WAL mode pragma is skipped when the backend is PostgreSQL
- Two transit instances running against the same PostgreSQL do not race on GC: only one runs per schedule tick
- Two transit instances appending to the same group log produce entries with distinct node_ids
- RUNBOOK.md includes Aurora Serverless v2 setup and a multi-instance deployment section
